paper_title: Probing MeV to 90 GeV axion-like particles with LEP and LHC
notes: Paper presents NEW measured exclusion limits from LEP data on Z→2γ and Z→3γ decays constraining axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to two photons (g_aγγ). The analysis fills a previously unexplored gap in the MeV to 10 GeV mass range. Two coupling scenarios are analyzed: (1) coupling to hypercharge bosons g_aBB (Fig. 4a) and (2) pure photon coupling g_aγγ (Fig. 4b). Data points extracted from Fig. 4(b) represent the pure photon coupling limits, which are the primary new result. The solid green line represents Z→3γ constraints (ma ≳ 10 GeV), and the dashed green line represents Z→2γ constraints (ma ≲ 10 GeV). Values are read from the log-log plot and represent approximate coupling limits at characteristic masses. The paper also discusses LHC projections (blue line in Fig. 4a) for the hypercharge coupling, but these are explicitly labeled as projections, not measured limits. The extraction confidence is moderate (0.75) because the exact numerical values must be read from a log-log plot rather than extracted from a table, introducing some uncertainty in the precise coupling values. | [VISION GATE C] extracted mass window is 7.6 dex outside the abstract-stated range [4e+09, 6e+10] eV — wrong figure/panel/regime traced
